newsitem.title: USA: E-Trade soars after stronger Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: E-Trade soars after stronger Q3 results.

text.p: Shares of E-Trade Group Inc. soared over 22 percent Wednesday after the company reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results despite an embarassing one-time charge.
"This was a very strong quarter in terms of the fundamentals overwhealming a pretty ugly one-time charge," said Keith Benjamin, an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co.
E-Trade said it took a one-time pre-tax charge of $4.3 million in connection with a clerical oversight in which it allowed its registration in Ohio to lapse.
The company said it has since automated the registration process to reduce the chances of repeating the error.

E-Trade, based in Palo Alto, Calif., provides services for trading securities over the Internet and through other electronic means. It reported earnings before the charge of $5.7 million, or 16 cents a share, well above the nine cent consensus estimate provided by First Call Inc.
Revenues rose 138 percent to a record $37 million from $15.5 million in the third quarter of fiscal 1996.
E-Trade's shares soared $4.50 on Nasdaq to $24.625 in active trading of more than four million shares, or roughly seven times the stock's normal daily volume over the last three months.

E-Trade's active customer accounts grew to 182,000 at the end of June, up 26 percent from 145,000 at the end of March and nearly 2.5 times the 74,000 it reported a year earlier -- extending its lead in Internet trading.
Benjamin said E-Trade currently accounts for 1 percent of the retail brokerage business and its business will benefit from the introduction in coming months of mutual funds and other services.
"Which means the 50 cent (earnings per share) number I have for next year could easily be 60 cents and in a strong market it might be 70 cents," he said.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said analyst Mark Wolfenberger,. citing the "blowout" fiscal third quarter results, raised his per share earnings estimate to 42 cents from 34 cents for fiscal 1997 and to 55 cents from 50 cents in fiscal 1998.
In the year ended September 1996, E-Trade had a loss of $838,000, or three cents a share, on revenues of $51.6 million.

E-Trade said its Web site continues to be the fastest-growing segment of its business, with an average of 9,600 transactions a day during the quarter, or 59 percent of total volume, and a 449 percent increase over a year ago.
